FINDINGS:

Severe tricompartmental joint arthrosis with intra-articular calcified body in the anterior aspect of the intercondylar groove

Fluid:
Small to moderate joint effusion with synovial hypertrophy. Prominent Baker's cyst measuring 33 x 16 mm, without signs of leakage or rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Severe chondropathy with diffuse chondral loss involving both articular surfaces and prominent subchondral reactive edema, without suggestive findings of subchondral insufficiency fractures. There is remodeling of the articular surfaces.
Unstable multidirectional complex tear of the medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion into the medial recesses.
No tears of the medial collateral ligament.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Moderate diffuse chondropathy with partial thickness chondral fissuring most pronounced on the weightbearing and posterior aspect of the femoral condyle and full-thickness fissuring involving the tibial weightbearing surface with mild subchondral reactive changes.
The lateral meniscus and collateral ligament complex are normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Moderate diffuse chondropathy with partial thickness chondral fissuring in both articular surfaces and mild subchondral reactive changes.
The extensor mechanism is normal. Fat stranding of the posterior aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.

Bones:
As described above Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Advanced tricompartmental osteoarthrosis of the right knee with severe diffuse chondropathy of the medial femorotibial compartment and prominent subchondral reactive bone marrow edema, without suggestive findings of insufficiency subchondral fractures. Small to moderate joint effusion with signs of synovial hypertrophy.
2.Unstable multidirectional tear of the medial meniscus.
3.Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Rule out meniscal tear.

PRIOR IMAGING: Plain film radiographs from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

T-TG distance is normal.

Lateral meniscus is intact. There is focal anterior and lateral femoral sulcus indentation with minor loss of cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle in the region of the sulcal depression. Overall articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

There is an oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus associated with a small posterior parameniscal cyst measuring about 4 to 5 mm in short axis tracking about 3 cm along the posterior margin of the meniscus and extending posterior to the base of the posterior cruciate ligament. Articular cartilage in the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is significant edema and soft tissue stranding extending from the space between the medial head of gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscle proximally into the popliteal fossa behind the distal femur and distally into the medial soft tissues of the calf deep to the pes anserine tendons. The finding is consistent with a ruptured Baker's cyst.

There is no significant knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION: 

Oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the medial meniscus involving body and posterior horn with associated para meniscal cyst posteriorly.

Nonacute osteochondral impaction injury involving lateral femoral sulcus with some mild focal cartilage loss overlying the region of cortical depression. No associated anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Soft tissue edema compatible with ruptured Baker's cyst.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Inestabilidad patelar.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Condropatía
superficial de la faceta lateral de la rótula.
Discreto aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Ligamento patelofemoral medial sin alteraciones.
No hay significativo derrame articular.
Discreto edema de la grasa prefemoral.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la faceta lateral de la rótula.
Probables fenómenos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula.
Discreto edema de la grasa prefemoral.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Chronic atraumatic knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small tricompartmental marginal osteophytes. Intraosseous ganglion cyst formation along the anterior medial tibial plateau.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Inner margin tearing of the body segment. Root attachments are intact. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: Scattered foci of high-grade cartilage loss along the weightbearing femoral condyle. High-grade cartilage loss at the periphery and anterior aspects of the tibial plateau with underlying subchondral cystic change/edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade chondrosis along the posterior weightbearing aspect of the femoral condyle along the intercondylar notch. Mild chondrosis along the posterior tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial thickness cartilage thinning along the inferior aspect of the lateral patellar facet with small areas of high-grade fissuring involving the medial facet. Foci of high-grade and full thickness cartilage loss along the medial and central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing along the medial distal fibers.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, mild to moderate in the medial compartment.
2.	Inner margin tearing of the medial meniscal body.
3.	Mild insertional quadriceps tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Artrosis de rodilla.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos impresionan de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Finas úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial, con fenómenos
condrales reparativos parciales regionales. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales sin alteraciones
significativas.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total de distribución difusa la articulación patelofemoral de predominio lateral
con cambios óseos secundarios predominando la región periférica lateral de la tróclea femoral.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa. Pequeño quiste poplíteo, con fenómenos de filtración hacia
cefálico y caudal.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales. Tendón rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps
femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Discreto edema las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 con fenómenos condrales reparativos de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 de la articulación patelofemoral, predominando en la región periférica
lateral de la tróclea femoral.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa. Pequeño quiste poplíteo con probable filtración.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales.
Discretos signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula y de fricción de la banda iliotibial,

> Status post left knee arthroscope.
* Osteophytes of left knee with wearing of articular cartilage, more prominent at lateral compartment, reflecting osteoarthritis.
  Focal linear hypointensity material in anterior intercondylar notch (Srs/Img: [ID].
* Irregular contour and increased signal intensity of the intra-articular cartilage of patella lateral and inferior part, in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
> Mild interstitial increased signal of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of mild degeneration. 
  PCL and MCL and LCL appear to be within normal.
* Joint effusion with mild increased signal intensity on T1WI and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae ; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. 
  Fat stranding of infrapatellar fat pad, with a increase signal intensity inside on PD F/S image, connected to suprapatellar bursa.
* Small size of lateral meniscus with linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Subcutaneous edema over left knee, prominent in prepatella region.
  Focal heterogeneous hyperintense foci at anterior and lateral peripatellar subcutaneous fat on T2WI and PD image (Srs/Img: 11/8-10), in favor of post-operative change  (s/p left knee arthroscope for 8 years)
> Small superficial nodular-like foci in infrapatellar region (Srs/Img: [ID]; 7,8/7), nature unknown?R/O granuloma or scar formation
IMP:
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at lateral compartment, with grade 3-4 chondral injury and loose body / detached cartilage.
2. Degeneration of lateral meniscus and R/O tear of posterior horn of lateral meniscus; differential diagnosis of  post-operative change ( partial menisectomy).
3. Synovitis- mild joint effusion of left knee with patellar plicae.
4. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL.   
5. R/O granuloma or scar formation over superficial skin.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management
